From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: buho

Spanish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • buho (pre-1952)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish buho, bufo, from Late Latin būfus, probably of onomatopoeic origin; see also Ancient Greek βοῦφος (boûphos).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbuo/ [ˈbu.o]
  • Audio (Spain):(file)
  • Rhymes: -uo
  • Syllabification: bú‧ho

Noun

[edit]

búho m (plural búhos)

  1. owl, eagle owl (any species of owl from the Strigidae family)
  2. (colloquial) informant, a squealer
    Synonyms: informante, delator

Derived terms

[edit]
  • búho cornudo
  • búho de anteojos
  • búho del desierto
  • búho lechoso
  • búho manchado
  • búho nival
  • búho penachudo
  • búho real

See also

[edit]
  • chucho
  • lechuza
  • tecolote

Further reading

[edit]
